meaning: Engulf weather reading: each day's forecast against past years, and what it means.
lead: 5 days away. Forecasts are getting firmer, and the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night is now in.
banner: Burn night is within a week, so this forecast is firming up. It gets more accurate every update until the burn.
summary: Expect afternoons around 65°, nights around 41°, and little rain. Day: long sleeves. Night: warm jacket, hat, gloves.
Burn night looks like light wind (around 4 mph), probably dry, and about 44° at the burns. Night: warm jacket, hat, gloves.

A normal Engulf week: afternoons around 72°, nights around 45°. It rains on about 1 in 7 days, frost comes about 1 in 10 nights, and wind at burn time rarely reaches 15 mph. Day: T-shirt. Night: warm jacket, hat, gloves; winter layers in a cold year.
When you'll know more: from about Nov 11, three days out, forecasts are usually within a few degrees.
why: The latest forecasts from the European and US weather services make up 94% to 100% of each day's numbers. This far out they're rough, so the rest is what a normal Engulf week looks like, from 30 years of records.
NOAA's longer-range outlook leans clearly warmer than normal for Nov 14–20, so the normal-year part of Saturday and Sunday is nudged that way.
The last month ran warm and dry, but that says little about any single day a week or more out, so it isn't in the numbers.
Each update leans more on the forecast; from a week out it's all forecast.

means: A big swing: 71° in the afternoon, about 54° after dark once the wind is counted, and near 45° by morning.
Gates open at 10 am, which leaves about 7 hours of daylight to set up.
Calm nights here often bring heavy dew: anything left out gets wet without rain.
